Is Your Business Sitting on Untapped Real Estate Value?

When you own the building your business operates from, you may be holding two very different assets: the business itself and the real estate underneath it.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

THE SHORT ANSWER

Before committing to a major renovation or sale, ask what the property would appeal to in today's market and what improvements buyers would actually pay for. In Tucson and Southern Arizona, local market knowledge matters: one neighborhood's opportunity may be another's overinvestment.

Separate the business from the real estate

When you own the building your business operates from, you may be holding two very different assets: the business itself and the real estate underneath it. That distinction matters when you're thinking about expanding, refinancing, selling, or planning your next chapter. A thriving business doesn't automatically mean the property is worth more, and a valuable property can sometimes be overlooked on the balance sheet.

Start with the property and the market

Start with the property, not just the business. Look at the location, building condition, land size, permitted uses, and what similar properties have sold for. For a business owner with a residential rental, home-based business property, or land with residential potential, an appraisal can help clarify the real estate's market value. Business goodwill, equipment, and operating profits are separate questions that may require other valuation specialists.

Evaluate improvements before committing

Before committing to a major renovation or sale, ask what the property would appeal to in today's market and what improvements buyers would actually pay for. In Tucson and Southern Arizona, local market knowledge matters: one neighborhood's opportunity may be another's overinvestment.
